notes: Complete, verbatim copy of Mailgun's official 'send' OpenAPI 3.1 document (the primary Mailgun API spec): messages, domains, events, stats, mailing lists, routes, webhooks, templates, etc. openapi.json is the upstream YAML rendered losslessly to JSON. Mailgun publishes three more OpenAPI 3.1 documents for the same API hosts (listed in documentation.mailgun.com/llms.txt) and, as of 2026-11-20, all are merged in: openapi.json = the send document plus every path, tag and component of upstream-validate.yaml (sha256:ead2649f…, 26 ops), upstream-inspect.yaml (sha256:6b44a403…, 59 ops) and upstream-optimize.yaml (sha256:855fc657…, 73 ops, whose 14 /v1/alerts/* operations are byte-identical to the send document's and are kept once); no path, operationId or component clashed, giving 411 operations (was 267). Shared component names (GenericResponse, string) are byte-identical across documents. The tool's re-derive (pnpm specs convert mailgun) rebuilds from upstream.yaml only, so redo this merge after any re-derive. Found via openfn-mocker/adaptors-storybook: snippets for the adaptor's validation calls hit /v4/address/validate*, which the send document lacks. MODIFICATION (overcommunicated): the published spec ships an EXAMPLE HTTP signing key placeholder that trips GitHub secret scanning; that one example value was replaced with 'key-REDACTED-EXAMPLE-SECRET' in upstream.yaml and openapi.json. It was documentation sample data, not a real credential; no path, operation, or schema is changed.
